amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي (25 مادة، بلا تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول) -- تصديقاً على نظام الهيئة العامة للأوقاف بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (73) وتاريخ 25/2/1437هـ. يحل محل نظام مجلس الأوقاف الأعلى الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/35) وتاريخ 18/7/1386هـ (م25/1)، ويُلغي ما يتعارض معه من أحكام نظام الهيئة العامة للولاية على أموال القاصرين الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/17) وتاريخ 13/3/1427هـ (م25/3، إلغاء جزئي مقيد بالتعارض).
عدّل صدر الفقرة (1) من المادة (السادسة) (صيغة تعيين رئيس المجلس)، بحسب نافذة "تعديلات المادة" على صفحة هيئة الخبراء -- غير منعكس في النص الرئيسي المعروض لهذه المادة على نفس الصفحة.
عدّل الفقرة الفرعية (1/و) من المادة (السادسة) (تمثيل المركز الوطني لتنمية القطاع غير الربحي بدلاً من ممثل وزاري)، بحسب نافذة "تعديلات المادة" -- غير منعكس في النص الرئيسي المعروض.
عدّل الفقرة الفرعية (1/ح) من المادة (السادسة) (تمثيل هيئة التراث بدلاً من ممثل وزارة السياحة)، بحسب نافذة "تعديلات المادة" -- غير منعكس في النص الرئيسي المعروض.
أعاد صياغة صدر الفقرة (1) من المادة (السادسة) إلى صيغة تعيين الرئيس بأمر من رئيس مجلس الوزراء (عكس تعديل القرار رقم 262)، بحسب نافذة "تعديلات المادة".

أضاف فقرة (2) إلى المادة (الحادية والعشرين) تستثني الوقف الخيري والحصة الخيرية في الوقف المشترك المسجلين لدى الهيئة من أحكام نظام التكاليف القضائية (بموجب توصية مجلس الوزراء رقم 363 وتاريخ 26/5/1444هـ بحسب مصادر ثانوية). هذا التعديل مُدرج في نص هذا المسار للمادة (الحادية والعشرين).

chapter_structure.label_ar: بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول
chapter_structure.title_ar: مواد متسلسلة غير مجمعة تحت أبواب أو فصول رسمية، لا يحمل أي منها عنواناً فرعياً في المصدر: تعريفات (م1) -- تأسيس الهيئة وشخصيتها الاعتبارية (م2) -- أهداف الهيئة (م3) -- الإشراف على الأوقاف والنظار (م4) -- مهمات الهيئة (م5) -- تشكيل مجلس الإدارة (م6) -- اختصاصات المجلس (م7) -- اجتماعات المجلس (م8) -- المحافظ واختصاصاته (م9) -- نائب المحافظ (م10) -- اللجنة الاستشارية (م11) -- لجنة الرقابة والمراجعة الداخلية: تشكيلها (م12) -- أهدافها (م13) -- مقابل أتعاب إدارة الهيئة للأوقاف (م14) -- استثمار أصول الأوقاف واستقطاعاتها (م15) -- حسابات الأوقاف الخاصة (م16) -- السنة المالية (م17) -- النظام المالي المحاسبي للأوقاف (م18) -- ميزانية الهيئة ومصادر إيراداتها (م19) -- مراجعة الحسابات (م20) -- معاملة الهيئة من حيث الرسوم واستثناء الوقف الخيري من التكاليف القضائية (م21) -- لائحة التوظيف وسريان نظامي العمل والتأمينات الاجتماعية (م22) -- الالتزام بشروط الواقفين وأحكام الشريعة (م23) -- حظر تعارض المصالح (م24) -- الإحلال محل نظام مجلس الأوقاف الأعلى، والنفاذ، والإلغاء (م25).

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable this pass for this law's exact detail URL (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/cabff788-438d-4003-be74-a9a700f2bcde/1), consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this BOE portal. Wayback Machine snapshots of this exact URL WERE reachable via direct curl (the WebFetch tool itself refused to fetch web.archive.org URLs in this environment -- "Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org" -- so snapshots were retrieved with curl over the pre-configured proxy instead, then parsed offline with BeautifulSoup, not a naive regex/tag-stripping approach). SIX independent snapshots spanning six years were fetched and diffed article-by-article: 20191121035643 (21 Nov 2019), 20220505003744 (5 May 2022), 20230927045754 (27 Sep 2023), 20240420035136 (20 Apr 2024), 20241203171652 (3 Dec 2024), and 20251212214335 (12 Dec 2025). All 25 'article_item' divs are present in every snapshot, in the same order, with the same two of them (Article 6 and Article 21) consistently carrying an additional 'changed-article' CSS class and a nested 'تعديلات المادة' (article amendments) changelog popup -- all other 23 articles carry only 'no_alternate' with no amendment marker and were found textually IDENTICAL (save for immaterial tashkeel/diacritic and list-numbering-prefix rendering differences in the earliest 2019 snapshot only) across all six time-points, strong evidence they remain unamended. This law has NO أبواب or فصول -- a flat sequence of 25 individually numbered articles, confirmed by the complete absence of any باب/فصل heading element anywhere in the archived HTML across all six snapshots. No article carries an inline topic title in the BOE source (every 'h3.center' heading is a bare ordinal followed only by a colon, e.g. 'المادة الأولى:') -- consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law and nazaha_law precedent for BOE sources lacking inline per-article titles; no title_ar key is used. DECREE IDENTIFICATION: this corpus's own coverage_gap_map.json entry for this law flagged genuine ambiguity ('estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/11 dated 26/2/1437H -- note: an earlier search hit suggested M/25, but M/11 is the better-attested number and should be the one verified before use'). This pass resolves this decisively: Royal Decree No. (م/11) dated 26/2/1437هـ (approving Council of Ministers Resolution No. 73 dated 25/2/1437هـ) IS the correct, current, sole organizing/establishing statute, confirmed via THREE independent sources: (1) BOE's own metadata panel for this law ("أدوات إصدار النظام": "مرسوم ملكي رقم (م/11) بتاريخ 26 / 2 / 1437"; "تاريخ الإصدار": 1437/02/26هـ الموافق 08/12/2015م; "تاريخ النشر": 1437/03/14هـ الموافق 25/12/2015م; "الحالة": ساري); (2) a WebSearch aggregation independently corroborating the same decree number/date and the same 25/12/2015G publication date; and (3) most decisively, the General Authority for Awqaf's OWN official website (web.awqaf.gov.sa) hosts a scanned PDF of this exact original Royal Decree and its underlying Council of Ministers Resolution -- fetched live this pass (2,585,104 bytes, 18 pages, an image-based/scanned PDF with no extractable text layer beyond its cover, so its content pages were read via direct visual inspection of the rendered page images, not OCR/pdftotext) -- showing Royal Decree No. م/11 dated 26/2/1437هـ, signed 'سلمان بن عبدالعزيز آل سعود' (King Salman), citing Council of Ministers Resolution No. 73 dated 25/2/1437هـ, and the resolution's own recital citations of نظام مجلس الأوقاف الأعلى (م/35، 1386هـ), نظام الهيئة العامة للولاية على أموال القاصرين (م/17، 1427هـ), and نظام المرافعات الشرعية (م/1، 1435هـ) -- each of which is INDEPENDENTLY re-confirmed by this same law's own clean (non-OCR) BOE-sourced Article 25 text, giving strong cross-validation of the visual-read preamble against a completely independent, high-confidence source. The earlier 'M/25' search hit noted in the gap-map is not corroborated by any source found this pass and appears to be an unrelated confusion (M/25 being a different Royal Decree number entirely, coincidentally the same number used for this corpus's own already-ingested nazaha_law track) -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key awqaf_gap_map_estimate_corrected_and_confirmed. TWO ARTICLES WITH CONFIRMED AMENDMENTS, TREATED DIFFERENTLY: Article 6 (board of directors composition) and Article 21 (fees) are the only two of 25 articles flagged 'changed-article' on BOE's page, each with its own 'تعديلات المادة' changelog popup quoting the amending Resolution/Decree text. For BOTH articles, BOE's own MAIN, primarily-displayed article body text is confirmed STALE relative to what the changelog itself describes -- verified by diffing all six snapshots (2019-2025), which show the exact same main-body text for each of these two articles throughout, including at snapshots that postdate every logged amendment by years. This track treats the two articles DIFFERENTLY given a material difference in how clean/reconstructible each changelog is: Article 21's changelog is a SINGLE, self-contained, fully-quoted replacement text (adding one new paragraph, with the complete post-amendment article quoted verbatim by BOE itself) -- following this corpus's accounting_auditing_law precedent for exactly this main-body-stale-vs-changelog-popup pattern, this track ingests that quoted amended text as Article 21's current text (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key awqaf_article21_changelog_amendment_incorporated_main_body_stale). Article 6's changelog instead describes FOUR separate, partial, layered substitution instructions across six years (Resolutions 262/1438H, 618/1442H, 638/1442H, 651/1443H) whose own quoted 'before' phrasing does not, on inspection, match the article's actual historically-observed original wording -- implying at least one additional, unlogged intermediate amendment this pass could not identify or verify. Hand-assembling a 'best guess' consolidated text from four partial, internally-inconsistent instructions would risk exactly the kind of fabrication this corpus's trust policy forbids, so this track instead ingests BOE's own stable, six-year-consistent main-body text for Article 6 as-is, marks it معدلة (since amendments are confirmed to exist even if not fully incorporated into the displayed text), records all four amendments in full in its history[] array, and flags the unresolved inconsistency explicitly (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key awqaf_article6_boe_main_body_not_reflecting_own_changelog) rather than silently merging or guessing. SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION: nezams.com (fetched live this pass) independently corroborates the decree number/date, the 25-article count, and -- critically -- the SAME four Council of Ministers Resolution numbers/dates for Article 6's amendment history (262/1438H, 618/1442H, 638/1442H, 651/1443H) and the same Royal Decree M/72 (1444/6/1H) reference for Article 21, giving independent confirmation that these amendments are real, dated, and correctly cited (though nezams.com's own page, like BOE's, was not observed to differ from BOE's main-body/changelog split). A further independent WebSearch aggregation corroborated Article 21's amendment via Council of Ministers Resolution 363 (26/5/1444H) and Saudi press coverage (alriyadh.com, 'استثناء الوقف الخيري من أحكام التكاليف القضائية') describing the same substantive exemption of charitable waqf from judicial-costs law -- an independent, non-BOE, non-nezams.com confirmation that this amendment is real and in force. A direct fetch of the Umm Al-Qura Gazette's own notice page (uqn.gov.sa/?p=21112) was attempted but returned only the gazette site's dynamic homepage shell (JavaScript-rendered, not directly scrapable this pass) rather than the specific notice text -- not pursued further per this corpus's stated 1-2-verification-attempts-per-fact policy, given the amendment was already independently corroborated by nezams.com and the WebSearch aggregation of press coverage. REPEAL / PREDECESSOR: this law's own Article 25(1) states, in its own BOE-sourced primary text: 'يحل هذا النظام محل نظام مجلس الأوقاف الأعلى الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/35) وتاريخ 18/7/1386هـ' -- i.e. it directly, explicitly replaces the Supreme Awqaf Council System (Royal Decree M/35, 18/7/1386H). This predecessor instrument's own separate BOE law-detail page was located via WebSearch this pass (lawId f804a9a7-503c-4ae0-afc2-a9a700f2bd73) but NOT independently fetched or read in full (out of scope; historical predecessor context only, not ingested as articles, consistent with this corpus's standard practice -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key awqaf_predecessor_m35_1386h_confirmed_primary). Article 25(3) further states this law repeals whatever OTHER provisions conflict with it, expressly naming نظام الهيئة العامة للولاية على أموال القاصرين ومن في حكمهم (Royal Decree M/17, 13/3/1427H) as one such instrument -- a conflict-only partial repeal, not a full supersession (that guardianship-of-minors law otherwise remains in force and is not ingested here); and Article 25(2) states this law's provisions govern Awqaf under the Authority's نظارة notwithstanding Article 223 of نظام المرافعات الشرعية (Royal Decree M/1, 22/1/1435H), a substantive procedural carve-out noted for completeness only. DISTINCTION FROM ANY SEPARATE SUBSTANTIVE WAQF LAW: per this track's task brief, this pass specifically searched for any DISTINCT, separately-codified 'نظام الأوقاف' governing the substantive law of endowments themselves (formation, conditions, termination of a waqf) as opposed to the Authority's own organizing/institutional statute. No such separate BOE-catalogued instrument was found. The only BOE-catalogued laws matching an 'أوقاف'-institutional naming pattern are this track's own subject law (نظام الهيئة العامة للأوقاف, the Authority's organizing statute -- mandate, board, budget, fee treatment) and its now-repealed predecessor (نظام مجلس الأوقاف الأعلى, M/35, 1386H) -- both organizing/institutional statutes, not substantive-waqf codes. Substantive waqf law in Saudi Arabia continues to be governed primarily by classical Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) as applied by the courts (per نظام المرافعات الشرعية procedure), not by a separate codified statute. This confirms the coverage-gap-map's implicit target IS this Authority's organizing statute, and that ingesting it does not omit or conflict with some separate substantive Waqf code (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key awqaf_distinct_from_any_separate_substantive_waqf_law). IMPLEMENTING REGULATIONS: this law's own text references several companion regulations to be issued by the Board (لائحة الاستثمار in Articles 7(6),(8),(9); لوائح إدارية ومالية واستثمارية in Article 7(3); لائحة التوظيف in Article 22(1)), and the Authority's own official website (web.awqaf.gov.sa/ar/Regulations, fetched live this pass) additionally lists standalone implementing instruments already issued: تعليمات الموافقة على إنشاء الصناديق الاستثمارية الوقفية (6 Oct 2022), لائحة إنشاء المحافظ الاستثمارية الوقفية (30 Apr 2023), and لائحة تنظيم أعمال النظارة (16 Oct 2023). Per this corpus's established one-Law-per-pass precedent (nazaha_law, accounting_auditing_law, and others), NONE of these are ingested this pass -- flagged as a candidate for a dedicated follow-up (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key awqaf_implementing_regs_not_ingested). No legal text is altered beyond whitespace/line-break normalization needed to render BOE's HTML as plain text (converting
to newlines; rendering Article 6's HTML of board-seat rows as one line per seat joined 'letter. role — membership-count', since the original is a literal three-column HTML table, not a single run of text) and, for Article 21 only, substituting BOE's own quoted changelog replacement text for its stale main body (see above). Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: CRITICAL -- this track's single most important documented discrepancy. Article 6 (مجلس الإدارة, board of directors composition) carries FOUR confirmed, dated amendments per BOE's own 'تعديلات المادة' changelog popup on this law's own law-detail page: (1) Council of Ministers Resolution 262, 2/5/1438هـ -- substituting 'برئاسة وزير العمل والتنمية الاجتماعية' for 'يشكل من رئيس يعين بأمر من رئيس مجلس الوزراء' in the opening of paragraph (1); (2) Resolution 618, 20/10/1442هـ -- amending subparagraph (1/و), substituting 'ممثل من المركز الوطني لتنمية القطاع غير الربحي' for what the changelog itself describes as 'ممثل وزارة الموارد البشرية والتنمية الاجتماعية'; (3) Resolution 638, 27/10/1442هـ -- substituting 'ممثل من هيئة التراث' for 'ممثل من وزارة السياحة' in subparagraph (ح); (4) Resolution 651, 22/11/1443هـ -- reverting the paragraph-(1) chair formula back to 'يشكل من رئيس يعين بأمر من رئيس مجلس الوزراء' (undoing amendment 1's substitution). Diffing all SIX independently-fetched Wayback snapshots of this exact BOE page spanning 21 Nov 2019 through 12 Dec 2025 shows the MAIN, primarily-displayed article body text for Article 6 has remained SUBSTANTIVELY UNCHANGED throughout this entire six-year window (only immaterial tashkeel/diacritic differences in the earliest 2019 snapshot) -- i.e., even the earliest observable snapshot (Nov 2019, itself years after amendment 1's 2017 resolution) already shows the SAME chair-formula wording as the most recent (Dec 2025, years after amendment 4's 2022 resolution), and subparagraphs (و) and (ح) have displayed 'ممثل من وزارة الشؤون الاجتماعية' and 'ممثل من الهيئة العامة للسياحة والتراث الوطني' respectively throughout -- NEITHER of which matches the 'before' phrasing the changelog itself quotes for amendments 2 and 3 ('ممثل وزارة الموارد البشرية والتنمية الاجتماعية' and 'ممثل من وزارة السياحة'), let alone the 'after' phrasing. This means BOE's own logged amendment history is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT with its own main-body text at every observed time-point, and implies at least one further, unlogged intermediate amendment step (most plausibly tied to the 2019-2020 restructuring of the former Ministry of Labor and Social Development into the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, and the 2020 splitting of the former Saudi Commission for Tourism and National Heritage into a separate Ministry of Tourism and Heritage Commission) that this pass could not identify or verify from any source consulted. Given this internal inconsistency, this track does NOT attempt to hand-reconstruct a speculative 'merged current' text for subparagraphs (و)/(ح) or the chair formula -- doing so would require guessing at an unverified intermediate state, which this corpus's trust policy expressly forbids ('never guess at an article's wording'). Instead this track ingests BOE's own stable, six-year-consistent main-body text as Article 6's 'text' field, marks legal_status_ar = معدلة (amendments are confirmed to exist per multiple independent sources, even though not fully incorporated into the displayed text), and records all four amendments in full, verbatim, in the article's own history[] array. nezams.com independently corroborates the same four resolution numbers/dates, but was not observed to resolve the inconsistency either. This is flagged here as the single highest-priority item for a dedicated, deeper follow-up pass -- ideally consulting the raw Umm Al-Qura Gazette issues for Resolutions 618 and 638 directly -- before this article's board-composition wording (subparagraphs و and ح specifically) is relied upon as definitively reflecting current law. BOE's own main-body article text for Article 6 is confirmed genuinely stale relative to the current, amended law -- not a proxy or reachability artifact -- since the same substantively unchanged wording persisted across all six independent snapshots spanning the entire 2019-2025 window despite four confirmed, dated amending resolutions during that period.

Article 21 (fee treatment) is the OTHER of only two articles BOE flags 'changed-article' on this law's page. Unlike Article 6, this article's changelog is a SINGLE, clean, self-contained, fully-quoted amendment: BOE's own 'تعديلات المادة' popup states 'إضافة فقرة تحمل الرقم (2) إلى هذه المادة وذلك بموجب المرسوم الملكي رقم (م/72) وتاريخ 1444/6/1هـ' and then quotes the COMPLETE resulting two-paragraph article text verbatim in full ('1- تعامل الهيئة من حيث الرسوم معاملة الهيئات والمؤسسات العامة. 2- يستثنى الوقف الخيري، والحصة الخيرية في الوقف المشترك، المسجلان لدى الهيئة، من أحكام نظام التكاليف القضائية'). Diffing all six independently-fetched Wayback snapshots (2019-2025), including four that POSTDATE this amendment by months to years (Sep 2023, Apr 2024, Dec 2024, Dec 2025), shows BOE's own MAIN, primarily-displayed article body text for Article 21 has remained the single-paragraph PRE-amendment wording throughout -- i.e. this stale-main-body pattern has persisted for at least 2+ years post-amendment across every checked snapshot. A WebSearch aggregation independently corroborated the substance of this amendment via Council of Ministers Resolution 363 (26/5/1444H) and Saudi press coverage (alriyadh.com's article headlined 'استثناء الوقف الخيري من أحكام التكاليف القضائية') -- an independent, non-BOE, non-nezams.com confirmation this amendment is real, dated, and in force. Following this corpus's established accounting_auditing_law precedent for exactly this main-body-stale-vs-changelog-popup pattern (which resolved it by ingesting the changelog-popup wording, not the stale main body, once independently cross-verified), this track ingests the quoted amended (two-paragraph) text as Article 21's current in-force text, marks legal_status_ar = معدلة, and records the amendment in full in the article's history[] array. A direct fetch of the Umm Al-Qura Gazette's own notice page for this amendment (uqn.gov.sa/?p=21112) was attempted but returned only the gazette site's dynamic homepage shell (not independently scrapable this pass) rather than the notice text itself; not pursued further per this corpus's 1-2-verification-attempts-per-fact policy, given the amendment was already corroborated by two independent non-BOE sources (nezams.com and the WebSearch/press aggregation).

This corpus's own reports/coverage_gap_map/coverage_gap_map.json entry for this law flagged genuine ambiguity: 'estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/11 dated 26/2/1437H (2016) -- note: an earlier search hit suggested M/25, but M/11 is the better-attested number and should be the one verified before use', and left 'estimated_article_count: Not confirmed -- needs verification'. This pass resolves and confirms this: Royal Decree No. (م/11) dated 26/2/1437هـ (approving Council of Ministers Resolution No. 73 dated 25/2/1437هـ), confirmed to contain exactly 25 articles with no أبواب/فصول subdivision, IS the correct and current organizing statute -- independently confirmed via BOE's own metadata panel, a WebSearch aggregation, and (most decisively) a scanned copy of the original Royal Decree and Council of Ministers Resolution hosted on the Authority's own official website (web.awqaf.gov.sa), read via direct visual inspection of the PDF's page images (an image-based/scanned PDF with no extractable text layer). The gap-map's noted 'M/25' search hit was NOT corroborated by any source consulted this pass; it appears to be an unrelated mix-up, since M/25 is a different Royal Decree number entirely -- coincidentally the same number this corpus's already-ingested nazaha_law track uses for a wholly unrelated statute (نظام هيئة الرقابة ومكافحة الفساد, dated 23/1/1446هـ, a full 30 hijri years later). No connection between that unrelated M/25 decree and this Awqaf-Authority law was found.

This law has NO أبواب (parts) or فصول (chapters) -- it is a flat sequence of 25 individually-numbered articles with no grouping/part headers anywhere on the BOE page across any of the six independently-fetched snapshots (no باب/فصل heading element was found alongside the 25 'article_item' divs in any snapshot). This track's chapter_structure field reflects this verified flat structure (a single leaf range 1-25) rather than inventing a topical grouping not present in the primary source, consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law precedent.

This law's BOE-hosted HTML supplies NO inline title text for any of its 25 articles -- every 'h3.center' heading for an article is a bare ordinal followed only by a colon (e.g. 'المادة الأولى:'), across all six snapshots checked. Consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law and nazaha_law precedent for BOE sources lacking inline per-article titles, no title_ar key is used for any article; section_ar instead carries the constant 'بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول' for structural context, since -- unlike nazaha_law -- this law has no أبواب at all.
